senses.gloss:
पुण् पुण् (connected with पुण्य, q. v.),
cl. 6. P. पुणति, पुणितुम्, to be pure or
virtuous; to do a pious or holy act; cl. 10. P.
पोणयति, -यितुम्, to collect, heap up, accumulate.

पूण् पूण् [cf. rt. पूल्], cl. 10. P. पूण-
यति, -यितुम्, to collect or heap together,
accumulate.

पुणतामकर पुणतामकर, अस्, m., N. of
the author of the Ātmatva-jāti-vicāra and Sādṛśya-
vāda, (also called Mahā-deva.)

पुण्ट् पुण्ट्, cl. 10. P. पुण्टयति, -यितुम्,
to speak; to shine.

पुण्ड् पुण्ड्, cl. 1. P. पुण्डति, पुण्डितुम्, to
rub, grind, pound, reduce to dust or powder.

पुण्ड पुण्ड, अस्, m. = पुण्ड्र, a mark, sign.
—पुण्ड-वर्धन = पुण्ड्र-वर्धन, q. v.

पुण्डरीक पुण्डरीक, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt.
पुण्), a lotus-flower, especially a white lotus, (used at
the end of an adj. comp. as expressive of beauty, see
Gaṇa Vyāghrādi to Pāṇ. II. 1, 56); a white umbrella;
a kind of drug; a mark on the forehead (in this
sense perhaps also m.); N. of a sacred bathing-place;
(अस्), m. a kind of sacrifice; a species of rice; a
fragrant kind of mango; Artemisia Indica (= द-
मनक); a variety of the sugar-cane; a silk-
worm (?); a kind of leprosy; fever in an elephant;
white (the colour); a tiger; a kind of serpent; N.
of a Nāga; a pitcher, student's water-pot; N. of
the elephant of the south-east quarter; N. of an
ancient king; of a son of Nabha or Nabhas; (with
Jainas) N. of a Gaṇa-dhara; N. of a hermit the son
of Śveta-ketu and Lakṣmī; of a mountain; (आ),
f., N. of an Apsaras; of a daughter of Vasiṣṭha
and wife of Prāṇa or Pāṇḍu.
—पुण्डरि-स्रजा,
f. (पुण्डरि substituted for पुण्डरीक), Ved. a
wreath or garland of lotuses.
—पुण्डरीक-नारद-
संवाद, अस्, m., N. of the thirty-second chapter
of the Pārtha Itihāsa-samuccaya.
—पुण्डरीक-प-
लाशाक्ष (˚श-अक्ष), अस्, ई, अम्, having eyes like
the petals of a lotus.
—पुण्डरीक-पुर, अम्, n.,
N. of a city.
—पुण्डरीक-प्लव, अस्, m. a kind of
bird.
—पुण्डरीक-मुखी, f. a kind of leech.
—पुण्डरीकाक्ष (˚क-अक्ष), अस्, m. ‘lotus-
eyed,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu; a kind of drug (=
पुण्डर्य, प्र-पौण्डरीक).
—पुण्डरीकात-
पत्र (˚क-आत्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, having the lotus for
an umbrella (said of the autumn).
—पुण्डरीकाव-
तंस (˚क-अव्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, having white lotus-
flowers for ear ornaments.
—पुण्डरीकोदर-प्र-
भ (˚क-उद्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, resplendent as the in-
terior of a white lotus.

पुण्डरीयक, अस्, m., N. of a divinity enu-
merated among the Viśve Devāḥ; (अम्), n. Ketmia
Mutabilis (= स्थल-पद्म); a kind of drug (com-
monly called पुण्डरीय).

पुण्डर्य, अम्, n. a creeper; a medicinal plant used
as a remedy for diseased eyes (= प्र-पौण्डरीक).

पुण्ड्र पुण्ड्र, अस्, m. a red variety of the
common sugar-cane, Saccharum Officinarum; a white
lotus, a lotus in general; a species of tree (= ह्रस्व-
प्लक्ष); a kind of creeper, Gærtnera Racemosa
(= अति-मुक्तक, वासन्ती); a mark or line made
on the forehead with sandal &c., sectarial mark; a
worm; N. of a Daitya or infernal being considered
incarnate in Śiśu-pāla; N. of a son of Bali; (आस्),
m. pl., N. of a people and of their country (the
modern Bengal and Behar, ‘the country of the
sugar-cane’); N. of a mythical city between the
mountains Hima-vat and Hema-kūṭa.
—पुण्ड्र-
केलि, इस्, m. an elephant.
—पुण्ड्र-देश, अस्, m.,
N. of a district.
—पुण्ड्र-नगर, अम्, n. ‘city of
the Puṇḍras,’ N. of a town; [cf. पौण्ड्रनागर.]
—पुण्ड्र-वर्धन, अम्, n., N. of a town in
Gauḍa; (also spelt पुण्ड-वर्धन.)

पुण्ड्रक, अस्, m. a red variety of the common
sugar-cane, Saccharum Officinarum; a kind of creeper,
Gærtnera Racemosa; a species of tree; a mark on
the forehead, sectarial mark; one who lives by
breeding silk-worms; N. of a man (?).

पुण्ढ्र, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), a mark, sign,
sectarial mark; [cf. पुण्ड्र.]

पुण्य पुण्य, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt.
1. पू; according to others fr. rt. 1. पुष् or rt.
पुण्; not met with in the earliest language), good,
pure, holy, right, righteous, virtuous, just, sacred;
happy, prosperous, favourable, propitious, auspicious,
lucky; bright, fine, beautiful, pleasing; sweet, fra-
grant (as an odour); solemn, festive, ferial; (अम्),
n. good, right, virtue, moral or religious merit; a
good or meritorious act; purity, purification; a reli-
gious ceremony, especially one performed by a wife
in order to retain her husband's affections and to
obtain a son; a brick trough for watering cattle, =
कोष्ठक; (अस्), m., N. of a man; of a lake (in
this sense perhaps n.); (आ), f. holy basil, Ocymum
Sanctum; N. of a daughter of Kratu and San-natī.
—पुण्य-कर्तृ, ता, m. ‘right-doer,’ an upright
or virtuous man.
—पुण्य-कर्मन्, अ, n. a virtuous
or meritorious act; (आ, आ, अ), whose actions are
holy or meritorious, doing good works, upright,
righteous, virtuous, pious; [cf. पुण्यैक-कर्मन्.]
—पुण्य-काल, अस्, m. an auspicious time.
—पु-
ण्यकाल-ता, f. a propitious period.
—पुण्य-कीर्त्ति,
इस्, इस्, इ, bearing a good name, famous, celebrated;
N. of a Buddhist (whose form was assumed by
Viṣṇu).
—पुण्य-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, ‘right-doing,’ up-
right, virtuous; N. of a divinity enumerated among
the Viśve Devāḥ.
—पुण्य-कृत्या, f. a good action.
—पुण्य-क्षय, अस्, m. decay or loss of religious
merit.
—पुण्य-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. a holy place or
district, a place by visiting which merit is acquired,
a place of pilgrimage.
—पुण्य-गन्ध, अस्, आ,
अम्, sweet-scented, fragrant; (अस्), m. the Campaka,
Michelia Champaka.
—पुण्य-गन्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, or
पुण्य-गन्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, sweet-scented, fragrant.
—पुण्य-गृह, अम्, n. a house of charity, an
alms-house; a temple.
—पुण्य-जन, अस्, m. a
good or pious or virtuous man; N. of a class of
supernatural beings; a Yakṣa or attendant of Kuvera
the god of wealth; a fiend, goblin, Rākṣasa.
—पु-
ण्यजनेश्वर (˚न-ईश्˚), अस्, m. ‘lord of the Yakṣas,’
Kuvera the Hindū deity of wealth.
—पुण्य-जल,
अस्, आ, अम्, containing pure water.
—पुण्य-जित,
अस्, आ, अम्, gained or attained by good works.
—पुण्य-तर, अस्, अम्, purer, holier.
—पुण्य-
तरी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to make purer
or cleaner.
—पुण्य-ता, f. or पुण्य-त्व, अम्, n.
purity, holiness.
—पुण्य-तीर्थ, अम्, n. a holy shrine
or place of pilgrimage.
—पुण्य-तृण, अम्, n. holy
grass; N. of the white variety of Kuśa grass.
—पुण्य-दर्शन, अस्, आ, अम्, of beautiful appear-
ance, beautiful; (अस्), m. the blue jay, = चाष;
(अम्), n. visiting holy shrines.
—पुण्य-दुह्, -धुक्,
क्, क्, yielding or granting happiness or beatitude.
—पुण्य-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of a grammarian.
[]
—पुण्य-नामन्, आ, m., N. of one of the attend-
ants of Skanda.
—पुण्य-पुण्य-ता, f. perfect holi-
ness.
—पुण्य-पुरुष, अस्, m. a godly or good
man, a man rich in moral merit.
—पुण्य-प्र-
ताप, अस्, m. the might and efficacy of virtue or
of the merit acquired by a course of virtuous acts.
—पुण्य-प्रद, अस्, आ, अम्, conferring merit,
meritorious.
—पुण्य-प्रसव, आस्, m. pl. (with
Buddhists) N. of a class of deities.
—पुण्य-फल,
अम्, n. the fruit or reward of good works or merito-
rious actions; (अस्), m. ‘having good fruit,’ the garden
of Lakṣmī; a grove.
—पुण्य-बल, अस्, m., N. of
a king of Puṇya-vatī.
—पुण्य-भरित, अस्, आ, अम्,
extremely blessed, abounding in holiness or bliss.
—पुण्य-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, or पुण्य-भाजिन्, ई, इनी, इ,
possessing happiness, partaker of bliss, happy; pos-
sessing merit, virtuous.
—पुण्य-भू, ऊस्, f. the holy
land of the Hindūs (bounded on the north by the
Himālayas, on the south by the Vindhya mountains,
and on the east and west by the sea, = Āryāvarta).
—पुण्य-भूमि, इस्, f. the holy land of the Hindūs
[cf. पुण्य-भू above]; the mother of a male
child.
—पुण्य-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, formed or con-
sisting of good.
—पुण्य-मित्र, अस्, m., N. of a
Buddhist patriarch.
—पुण्य-योग, अस्, m. the influ-
ence or effect of virtuous actions done in a former
life.
—पुण्य-रात्र, अस्, m. a good or auspicious
night; a night on which any religious commemora-
tion or ceremony is held; [cf. पुण्याह.]
—पुण्य-
राशि, इस्, m., N. of a man; N. of a mountain.
—पुण्य-लब्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, attained by good
works (as a reward in heaven).
—पुण्य-लोक, अस्,
आ, अम्, belonging to a better world, sharing in a
better world (Ved.); (अस्), m. heaven, paradise.
—पुण्यलोक-त्र, ind., Ved. in a better world.
—पुण्य-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing merit, merito-
rious, pure, holy, righteous, pious, virtuous; pleasing,
beautiful; fortunate, lucky, auspicious; happy; (अती),
f., N. of a country.
—पुण्य-वर्धन, अम्, n.,
N. of a town; (probably a wrong reading for
पुण्ड्र-वर्धन.)
—पुण्य-वर्मन्, आ, m., N.
of a prince of Vi-darbha.
—पुण्य-वाग्-बुद्धि-
कर्मिन्, ई, इणी, इ, pure in word, thought, and deed.
—पुण्य-विजित, अस्, आ, अम्, acquired by merit,
merited.
—पुण्य-शकुन, अस्, m. a bird of good
omen.
—पुण्य-शाला, f. a house of charity, alms-
house.
—पुण्य-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, being of a virtuous
disposition, disposed to virtuous acts, virtuous, pious,
righteous.
—पुण्य-श्री-गर्भ, अस्, m., N. of a
Bodhi-sattva.
—पुण्य-श्लोक, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘well
spoken of,’ of good fame or reputation; (अस्), m. an
epithet of Nala; of Yudhi-ṣṭhira; of Kṛṣṇa; (आ),
f. an epithet of Draupadī; of Sītā.
—पुण्यश्लोक-
दिदृक्षा, f. the desire of seeing Nala.
—पुण्य-
श्लोक-पराङ्मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, having the face
averted from Nala.
—पुण्य-सञ्चय, अस्, m. a
store of virtue or religious merit.
—पुण्य-सम,
अम्, n. a good year.
—पुण्य-सार, अस्, m., N. of
a prince.
—पुण्य-सुन्दर, अस्, m., N. of a gram-
marian who arranged the Dhātu-pāṭha of Hema-
candra's grammar in alphabetical order.
—पुण्य-
सेन, अस्, m., N. of a man; of a prince of Ujjayinī.
—पुण्य-स्तम्भ-कर, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—पुण्य-स्थान, अम्, n. a sacred place, conse-
crated ground.
—पुण्यात्मन् (˚य-आत्˚), आ, आ, अ,
pure-souled, righteous, virtuous, pious, holy.
—पु-
ण्यालङ्कृत (˚य-अल्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, adorned by
virtue; (अस्), m., N. of a demon.
—पुण्याह (˚य-
अह), अम्, n. a good or happy or auspicious day,
holiday; पुण्याहं वच् in Caus., to wish any one
a happy or pleasant day.
—पुण्याहन् (˚य-अहन्),
अ, n., Ved. = पुण्याह above.
—पुण्याह-वाचन,
अम्, n. the declaration of a holiday, repeating at
sacrifices &c. ‘this is a holiday’ three times, wishing
any one a happy day.
—पुण्यैक-कर्मन् (˚य-
एक्˚), आ, आ, अ, one whose actions are only virtuous.
—पुण्योदका (˚य-उद्˚), f. ‘having sacred waters,’
N. of a river in the next world.
—पुण्योदय (˚य-
उद्˚), अस्, m. the resulting of good fortune (as the effect
of virtuous acts done in a former life).
—पुण्योद्यान
(˚य-उद्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, having beautiful gardens.

पुण्यक, अम्, n. a religious ceremony, festival;
a meritorious act or obligation of a religious nature
(as fasting, praying, &c.); a ceremony performed by
a woman in order to retain her husband's affections
and to obtain a son; the observance of this cere-
mony; the present made to a wife on that occasion.
—पुण्यक-व्रत, अम्, n. the worship of Kṛṣṇa
for a year, with daily presents, to be performed by a
woman desirous of a son.
